Daily Brief

The global news agenda today is dominated by political upheaval across multiple continents. In Washington, President Trump elevated hardliner Stephen Miller to White House Chief of Staff following the Republican midterm defeat, signaling a combative posture toward the new Democratic Congress [BBC, Le Monde, The Hindu]. In South America, Paraguay's President Santiago Peña was impeached and placed under house arrest after the collapse of Ueno Bank left millions locked out of their savings, marking only the second presidential removal in the country's post-dictatorship history [BBC, Globe and Mail, The Hindu]. Markets showed signs of stabilization after a brutal tech sell-off wiped trillions from AI and semiconductor stocks, though Asian and European indices remained under pressure [BBC, Le Monde]. European aviation faced a third consecutive wave of bomb threats affecting flights across Portugal, Italy, Czech Republic and Bulgaria, with a Russian extremist group denying involvement [BBC, France 24]. Meanwhile, New Zealand awaits final election results as neither major party appears able to form a government outright, with an estimated 700,000 special votes still to be counted [ABC Australia, RNZ, The Hindu].

Top Stories
01 Geopolitics

Paraguay's President Peña Impeached and Arrested After Bank Collapse Locks Out Millions

  • The Paraguayan Senate unanimously voted to remove President Santiago Peña from office following the collapse of Ueno Bank, which left nearly half the country's 6 million citizens unable to access their accounts
  • Peña was placed under house arrest on charges including breach of trust, influence peddling, and misappropriation of funds; he previously held shares in the company that owned the bank
  • Vice President Pedro Alliana was sworn in as interim president and pledged support for affected depositors
  • This marks only the second presidential impeachment in Paraguay since the end of General Stroessner's 35-year dictatorship in 1989

02 Policy

Trump Appoints Stephen Miller as Chief of Staff in Post-Midterm Shakeup

  • President Trump named Stephen Miller, architect of aggressive immigration enforcement policies, as White House Chief of Staff, replacing Susie Wiles
  • The appointment follows the Republican Party's sweeping defeat in Tuesday's midterm elections, which gave Democrats control of both chambers of Congress
  • Miller described his mission as fighting 'with all of our soul to support our president and defend this magnificent republic'
  • The move signals Trump is preparing for confrontation rather than compromise with the new Democratic Congress

Tech Stocks Partially Recover After Trillion-Dollar AI Sell-Off

  • The Nasdaq Composite rebounded 1.1% on Friday after falling 5.5% the previous day in a sell-off that wiped trillions from AI and technology stock valuations
  • Investors had sold tech shares partly due to concerns that Democratic midterm victories would slow artificial intelligence development
  • US employment figures showed an unexpectedly strong 165,000 jobs added in September, providing a mixed economic picture

Third Wave of Bomb Threats Disrupts European Airlines and Media Organizations

  • Multiple flights to and from Lisbon, Rome, Prague and Sofia were targeted with bomb threats on Friday, the third such wave this week
  • Three planes were escorted by Hungarian fighter jets; no explosives have been found on any aircraft
  • Irish media organizations including RTÉ, the Irish Independent, and radio stations were evacuated after receiving similar threats
  • A Russian extremist group named in some threats, the 'Male State,' denied involvement; UK authorities have called the incidents a 'malicious hoax'

05 Geopolitics

New Zealand Election Too Close to Call as Major Parties Struggle to Form Government

  • With over 98% of voting places counted, neither the National Party nor Labour has secured enough seats to form a government alone, with both hovering just under 30%
  • National lost several senior MPs including deputy leader Nicola Willis and Minister of Justice Paul Goldsmith
  • An estimated 700,000 special votes remain to be counted, which could take weeks to finalize results
  • The campaign was dominated by cost-of-living concerns amid high unemployment and the impact of global fuel shocks from the West Asia conflict
